newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - May 27.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - May 27.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$18.92 (-0.40)

BHP shares fell sharply after the company foreshadowed a flat performance until it restructured and new projects were commissioned. It also said there would be a number of abnormal adjustments to the full year to May 31 results, due on June 27, and that some would have an adverse impact. Managing director John Prescott said any substantial profit contributions from new projects in zinc, diamond and platinum mining, steelmaking and mineral sands were a year or more away. The stock ended off its lows, having been down 57 cents at one point.
As BHP sagged on Monday, investors were seen switching into alternative resource stocks.
* Australia and New Zealand Banking Group A$8.53 (+0.215)

ANZ performed strongly ahead of the release of its half year earnings on Wednesday. Analysts expect the bank to post a net profit of between A$580 and A$630 million for the six months to March 31, up from A$520 million for the previous corresponding period.

The Australian government continued to attack the big banks for not passing on all of Friday's 0.5 point rate cut in their variable home mortgage rates. Speaking in Parliament, Treasurer Peter Costello said consumers should place pressure on the banks by taking their business to alternative institutions with better deals.
Building stocks performed strongly following Friday's rate cut, led by Adelaide Brighton which announced the US$25.8 million sale of Hawaiian Cement to concentrate on its core activities.

National Mutual is tipped to report a small rise in half-year net profit on Tuesday, reflecting better investment returns and lower costs. Insurance analysts expect the French controlled insurer to report a net profit of between A$116 million and A$153 million for the six months ended March 31.
